evidence.claim: Ecovyst describes itself as a leading provider of virgin sulphuric acid, sulphuric-acid regeneration services, and sulphuric-acid derivatives, with products and services supporting industrial processes and materials tied to electrification.

Ecovyst's 2025 10-K summary describes the company as a leading provider of virgin and regenerated sulphuric-acid products and services, and notes that it provides regeneration services and purchases by-product sulphur from customers for use in manufacturing virgin sulphuric acid.
Ecovyst market capitalization was approximately USD 1.43B at the time of the June 8, 2026 finance snapshot.

Taseko's Florence Copper operation uses in-situ copper recovery and SX/EW processing and is designed to produce LME Grade A copper metal on site, with fully operational production capacity of 85 million pounds per year and a 22-year mine life.
Taseko announced in May 2026 that Florence Copper has a fixed-price contract in place for all sulphuric-acid requirements for 2026.

LSB Industries' corporate profile says it manufactures and sells nitrogen-based chemical products and offers various concentrations of nitric acid, sulphuric acid, mixed acids, ammonium nitrate solution, and anhydrous ammonia for industrial markets.
LSB Industries market capitalization was approximately USD 888M at the time of the June 8, 2026 finance snapshot.

memory_update.text: ECVT should be tracked as a direct underfollowed US-listed sulphuric-acid/regeneration platform; next layer should verify realized pricing, sulphur feedstock sourcing, and materiality of mining/electrification demand.
TGB is a clean downstream acid-access test case because Florence Copper is SX/EW/ISCR and Taseko disclosed fixed-price coverage for all 2026 sulphuric-acid requirements; verify 2027+ exposure.
LXU enters as a small-cap hypothesis: it sells sulphuric acids, but the revenue/materiality and sulphur input pass-through need verification before it survives Layer 2.

Integrated copper smelters with by-product acid and downstream SX/EW operators with contracted acid access should be separated from acid-import-dependent SX/EW operators; the direction of benefit can invert based on net acid balance.

US-listed pure sulphuric-acid logistics/storage assets appear scarce; several relevant acid distributors/terminals are private or non-US-listed, so public-market mapping may require indirect logistics names or foreign/OTC screens in later passes.

node: Sulphur and sulphuric acid supply chain for copper, nickel HPAL, and fertilizers
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid shock with a two-lane funnel. The reference lane keeps Southern Copper as a high-attention anchor because integrated smelting can create sulphuric-acid by-product/captive-supply dynamics. The underfollowed lane prioritizes Ecovyst as a direct North American sulphuric-acid/regeneration platform, Taseko as an acid-consuming SX/EW copper operator with a disclosed 2026 fixed-price acid contract, and LSB Industries as a small-cap industrial/agricultural chemicals producer that sells sulphuric acids but still needs verification on feedstock exposure and pricing pass-through. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
